item.title: Flight passenger's odd appearance at major US airport leads officers to wild discovery
item.description: Photos show cylindrical containers holding 10 live birds allegedly sewn into a flight passenger's underwear on an airplane that arrived in Miami from Havana, Cuba.
item.content:encoded:
A traveler's arrival at a Florida airport took an unusual turn after customs officers noticed something suspicious during an inspection.

U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) officers at Miami International Airport spotted what court documents described as an "unexplained bulge" around a passenger's waist and pelvic area after he arrived on a flight from Havana, Cuba, according to a federal complaint obtained by Fox News Digital.

A closer inspection allegedly uncovered 10 live birds concealed beneath the traveler's clothing, the complaint said.

AIRPORT X-RAY REVEALS SHOCKING ILLEGAL STASH CONCEALED BESIDE PASSENGER'S XBOX

Alberto Hernandez Castillo, a native of Cuba and legal permanent resident of the United States, arrived in Miami on Oct. 4. 

CBP officers selected him for a secondary inspection.

Castillo signed a customs declaration indicating he was not bringing animals or wildlife into the United States, according to court documents.

Officers first searched a carry-on bag and fanny pack belonging to Castillo but did not find any contraband.

During routine questioning about his trip, officers noticed the bulge beneath his clothing and said Castillo "appeared nervous" — prompting them to conduct a pat-down.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

The search allegedly revealed six clear cylindrical containers holding live birds. 

The containers were wrapped in tape and tucked inside black pockets sewn into his underwear, according to the complaint.

Officers recovered 10 birds from the containers, which were preliminarily identified as eight yellow-faced grassquits and two blue grosbeaks, court documents said.

Photos included in the complaint show the containers after they were removed, as well as how they were allegedly concealed beneath the man's clothing.

When questioned about the birds, Castillo allegedly told authorities they were for his "personal use."

He later invoked his right to remain silent, according to the complaint.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

Investigators said a records check found no indication that Castillo had filed the documentation required to legally import wildlife into the United States.

He was charged with smuggling goods into the United States, according to the federal complaint.

Court records recommend a $25,000 personal surety bond for Castillo.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

There is no evidence, "based on the records available at the time of inspection," that the man "submitted the documentation required for the lawful importation of wildlife," according to the complaint. 

The individual is due back in court on Oct. 26, according to the complaint.

Fox News Digital reached out to the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida for further details.

item.title: Woke Kasnas City radio host admits OutKick is right, but asks his listeners to not read us
item.description: A Kansas City Chiefs radio host says he agrees with OutKick's Josh Simmons reporting but claims he doesn't respect the platform or its coverage.
item.content:encoded:
A Kansas City sports radio host is unhappy with OutKick's coverage of the Chiefs. He says he doesn't disagree with anything we've written or reported, however. Instead, he claims he doesn't like that we're allowed to talk about his team while holding different views than he does.

On Tuesday, Carrington Harrison criticized members of the Kansas City sports media for "spending any part of [their] day arguing with Bobby Burack about any subject." In doing so, he spent part of his day posting about me on social media – and discussing OutKick and me on his radio show.

"I wouldn't get my [Chiefs] stories from OutKick," he said. "They are an underling of Clay Travis."

He then said he doesn't "respect OutKick."

Harrison later asked to appear on the conservative radio show Mundo in the Morning on KCMO in Kansas City. He claimed his issue with OutKick stemmed from a story we published last week about Chiefs left tackle Josh Simmons, who has yet to play this season.

In our story, we mentioned that ESPN had reported several "red flags" about Simmons' character and maturity before the 2024 draft. We also cited a Sports Illustrated report that Simmons left the team unannounced the night before a game last season, was unresponsive, and left the team unaware of his whereabouts for a period of time. Simmons then missed a month of games for what the team described as "personal" reasons.

This season, Simmons has missed all four of the Chiefs' games. The team says he has a back injury, one that team sources told multiple reporters was a non-issue in August. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler has since described the injury as "mysterious." Most other national insiders won't discuss the injury, even during injury roundup segments in which they cover minor ailments involving players of far less consequence.

We pointed out how the situation is unusual, that the team's lack of transparency is generating online theories, and that the secrecy suggests something more complicated than a simple back injury.

So, what exactly does a radio host on the Kansas City Chiefs' official station dispute about our analysis?

Well, nothing.

"I don't fundamentally disagree with Bobby Burack," Harrison told a perplexed Pete Mundo on Wednesday. "I would define someone who is a hater, who is someone who is incapable of giving credit when credit should be due."

Uh, okay.

"The truth doesn't matter who says the truth. It's still the truth regardless of who says it," he added.

So why the tweets, radio segments, and name-calling?

According to Harrison, he doesn't like that OutKick told the truth. What does that mean? Didn't he just say the opposite? We'll let him explain.

TOMI LAHREN DEFENDS OUTKICK'S ESPN SCOOP, TORCHES JEMELE HILL, BACKS SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM

"I don't respect Bobby Burack's reporting," he said. "I don't respect the platform that he has created for himself. I believe that he is somebody who has cultivated an audience and a brand around insects, bots, trolls and racists. That's not someone that I'm super interested in getting on the internet and having to tussle with and going back and forth with."

To recap, Carrington Harrison says he agrees with my reporting but doesn't respect it. He says he doesn't want to get into a back-and-forth with me, despite initiating a back-and-forth with me on X, his radio show, and another radio show.

At this point, you have to wonder if there is something seriously wrong with this guy. He certainly doesn't appear to be operating with the highest IQ.

Befuddled by Harrison's contradictions, Mundo questioned his premise.

"But you are saying that he is absolutely onto something there with this Josh Simmons thing, but then saying on the other hand, he's not credible on this situation," Mundo said.

"I've seen, I mean, I never said he's not credible on this situation. I've seen his work in reporting in other situations. That's just not somebody that I would align myself with," Harrison responded.

Huh?

Who asked him to align himself with anyone? He began by saying OutKick is not credible when it comes to the Chiefs, a point he now claims wasn't his intention.

He then reiterated exactly what we wrote last week.

"So in this situation, is there something greater going on with Josh Simmons? Yes, I 100% agree with that. Yes, I absolutely think there is something going on."

Mundo again questioned why Harrison had made a point of telling his listeners not to trust OutKick when he now confirmed that he agreed with exactly what we had reported about the subject.

"My sense of it is that you don't really disagree with Bobby. And I've only got about a minute here. You don't disagree with Bobby, but you kind of don't like Bobby and that's fine."

"That's your prerogative. I'm not saying you have to like him or not, but because you don't like him, you kind of want to twist them here or tweak them a little bit here in this whole deal. Is that a fair analysis of this situation?"

Harrison didn't deny it. Instead, he took more personal shots.

"I mean, I wouldn't say that I want to tweak him a little bit, but I think Bobby's problem is, I think Bobby has stood on the shoulder of giants and thinks that he's now tall. Bobby Burack has never done anything outside of the success of Clay Travis. So I don't want him to come on here and on your show and act like he is a top-notch investigator or reporter. That's definitely not true."

For the record, I did not claim to be an investigative reporter. My coverage of Josh Simmons is actually quite benign. I simply said the situation doesn't make much sense. I said that because the people covering the Chiefs daily, like Harrison, have been too afraid to do so at the risk of upsetting team public relations.

Now that we've gotten that out of the way, Harrison's comments raise a broader issue.

Why would a sports station in Kansas City tied to an NFL franchise want a host on the air who openly admits that he cannot tolerate the sports opinions of people who disagree with him politically?

Harrison confirmed on multiple occasions since Tuesday that he told his listeners to ignore OutKick's accurate information because he thinks our readers are racist and because of our association with Clay Travis, one of the country's most prominent conservative radio talk show hosts.

Imagine hosting a sports show in another city and saying something similar about a liberal outlet, while acknowledging their information is accurate.

Harrison sent a message to sports fans across Kansas and Missouri: If you are not as liberal as he is, you are not welcome to listen to his show.

Two points on that.

One, based on his numbers, most people aren't listening to his show anyway.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Two, OutKick asked the program director of his station, Steven Spector, whether Harrison's views about conservatives and OutKick represent the views of 96.5 The Fan.

Spector did not return our email in time for publication. We will update this story if he does. We also reached out to Harrison to see if he stands by his bizarre commentary.

Anyway, we at OutKick do not believe you have to vote a certain way to have an opinion about sports. We also stand by our coverage of Josh Simmons.

The starting left tackle for the NFL's most valuable asset playing in just eight games over two years, under two different sets of mysterious circumstances, is a story worth covering.

According to one Kansas City radio host, however, such coverage is only worthwhile if it comes from someone with the proper political leanings.

item.title: Jewish student sues New York school on Oct 7 anniversary over 'relentless antisemitic harassment'
item.description: Student Sophie Shabot alleged antisemitic assault and harassment at The New School's Parsons School of Design in a new lawsuit by The Lawfare Project.
item.content:encoded:
The Lawfare Project announced on the third anniversary of the deadly Oct. 7 Hamas attacks on Israel that it filed a lawsuit against The New School on behalf of a Jewish Israeli-American student it alleged faced "relentless antisemitic harassment, intimidation, and physical assault" as a student at the New York university.

According to the legal group, New School student Sophie Shabot faced numerous instances of name-calling, intimidation and obstruction based on her religion and support for Israel at the Parsons School of Design. She was reportedly called names like "Zio b----" and "baby killer" and prevented from entering the University Center.

In another instance, protesters allegedly vandalized and disrupted a Hillel event featuring an Israeli speaker in 2024. Shabot was among several Jewish students who were trapped in a dean's office as a group of protesters attempted to have them turn over the speaker.

JEWISH CAMPUS LIFE AT A ‘CROSSING POINT’ AS STUDENTS WEIGH ANTISEMITISM RISKS, NEW REPORT SHOWS

According to The Lawfare Project, university officials failed to stop the harassment against Shabot and other Jewish students and even "at times rewarded those responsible."

"There is no question in my mind that the New School violated its Title VI obligations and other obligations under the law in not intervening and taking meaningful action to stop the antisemitic, anti-Israeli harassment that my plaintiff endured while she was at the New School," Lawfare Project director of litigation Ziporah Reich told Fox News Digital.

Reich, who also filed the lawsuit, added that more often than not, Jewish students like Shabot were the ones who faced consequences at universities following antisemitic actions by other students.

"If the pro-Hamas protesters are essentially threatening your physical safety when you're trying to have a Jewish event, let's just shut down the event to make sure you're safe. When a group of pro-Hamas protesters occupy a space in which you're supposed to have an event, let's just move you somewhere else to a smaller, less accommodating place. In other words, she was bearing the brunt of the consequences for the negative harassment of the offenders," Reich said.

JEWISH UCLA STUDENTS BEATEN WITH STICKS, PEPPER SPRAYED AND KNOCKED OUT BY ANTI-ISRAEL CAMPUS MOB: LAWSUIT

Reich also acknowledged the significance of filing the lawsuit Wednesday on the anniversary of the attacks that killed more than 1,200 people in Israel and led to more than 250 people being abducted.

"It's extremely important for the Jewish community to recognize that what happened immediately after Oct. 7 didn't end immediately after Oct. 7 because the harassment of Jewish students and Jews everywhere has continued and even if it has lessened to some extent in certain universities, it has not gone away. It's essentially in a quiet period where we know that at any minute it can rear its ugly head again. These students are activists without a cause," Reich said.

The lawsuit brings claims under Title VI, New York state and city civil and human rights laws and claims for breach of contract and negligent infliction of emotional distress. It is seeking damages, statutory penalties, attorneys’ fees and costs, and other relief and demands a jury trial.

Fox News Digital reached out to The New School for comment but did not immediately receive a response. 

ANTI-ISRAEL NYC PROTESTERS CHANT SUPPORT FOR HAMAS, DEMAND MAMDANI MAKE MAJOR CHANGES AT RALLY

The New School's Parsons School of Design was previously sued by the Dhillon Law Group in 2025 over similar allegations made by graduate Brandon White. White claimed that the school had opened a disciplinary investigation against him after he reported incidents of harassment while his assailants received no retaliation.

The New School was also one of multiple universities overtaken by anti-Israel protesters after the Hamas terror attacks on Israel. In 2024, protesters occupied the Welcome Center in Manhattan to get the school's board of trustees to vote on divesting from companies supporting Israel. This came amid two encampments on campus, with one led by students and one led by faculty.

item.title: Unearthed clip exposes how far Talarico was willing to go on raising taxes during COVID era
item.description: James Talarico once said he didn't care what taxes had to be raised to avoid healthcare cuts in Texas during the COVID-19 budget shortfalls.
item.content:encoded:
James Talarico, the Democratic nominee for the Senate in Texas, once pressed Democrats to consider cuts to healthcare benefits a nonstarter — regardless of the consequences for the state’s finances.

The remark came during a podcast interview in which Talarico discussed how Texas might balance its budget amid COVID-related shortfalls. He feared Republicans would look for savings in healthcare services.

"I don't care where you get the revenue. I don't care what taxes you have to raise," Talarico said in a 2020 appearance with Texas Rising, a progressive YouTube channel focused on political engagement among younger voters.

The resurfaced moment adds to the pile of past statements dealing with gender, immigration and fiscal management, complicating the political calculus for Talarico as he aims to convince voters in Texas that he could represent a Republican-leaning constituency, even as a Democrat.

TALARICO SAYS HE 'MISSED THE MARK' AS HE BACKTRACKS ON CONTROVERSIAL WOKE STATEMENTS

At the time, Texas was facing a bleak financial outlook.

The pandemic had crippled key sections of the state’s regular revenue streams. As oil demand crashed nationally, tax revenue that would normally come from hotels, bars and restaurants also faced steep reductions. Texas Comptroller Glenn Hegar projected a $4.6 billion shortfall.

"The economic contraction associated with COVID-19 has resulted in revenue collection this fiscal year that is much lower than our earlier projections," Hegar said in a statement.

"This estimate also assumes that restrictions on businesses and individuals will be lifted before the end of this calendar year and that economic activity will strengthen."

As a part of the COVID response, Texas ordered most agencies to look for ways to cut their spending by 5% in the 2020 – 2021 budget.

In a letter, Governor Greg Abbott largely shielded Health and Human Services (HHS) from the reductions, sparing the state’s Medicaid program, the Children’s Health Insurance Program, the foster care program and disability services, among others. Even so, $2.6 billion of HHS’s budget remained subject to cuts, according to the agency's estimations.

That left the Health and Human Services Commission with a target of $132,716,600 in cuts.

'FAKE' MODERATE TALARICO'S TEXAS SURGE TESTS PAXTON IN FIGHT TO HOLD CRUCIAL GOP SENATE SEAT

Despite the reduced figure, Talarico blasted the idea of making spending reductions geared towards healthcare.

"You're not going to make our students and our teachers — you're not going to make the sick and the elderly pay for this pandemic we are not going to balance our budget off of the most vulnerable people in this state," Talarico said.

He argued that Democrats should create a similar kind of stigma against cuts to HHS as the one surrounding raising taxes.

"Sometimes you get the reaction in the capitol that's an unreasonable position to take. But the other side of the aisle has already taken revenue increases off the table. They've done a good job of making certain options taboo, so I think our coalition, not just Democrats but progressives, and anybody with a functioning heart should be able to make cuts to health and education taboo and take them off the table," Talarico said.

The moment has brought on criticisms from at least one Republican onlooker.

"High-tax Talarico never saw a tax hike he didn't love in the Texas Legislature, and he is promising to continue that if elected to the Senate. James Talarico will raise taxes on every Texan to fund his radical agenda of taxpayer-funded sex changes for kids and free healthcare for illegal immigrants," Zach Kraft, a spokesperson for the Republican National Committee said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

As he wages his bid for U.S. Senate, Talarico has advocated for an expansion of U.S. health policy.

On his website, Talarico has called for universal eligibility for Medicare, to regulate medical debt and expand veteran care. His views on Medicare, which overlap with many other progressives in the party, have prompted criticism from Republicans who believe such an expansion would cripple the federal budget with cost.

Skeptics of the plan have argued for years that such an expansion is too expensive and does little to address existing inefficiencies in the American healthcare system.

In 2019, Sen. John Barrasso, R-Wyo., took to the Senate floor to blast the idea, calling it a straitjacket solution that would undermine healthcare quality.

"The [Congressional Budget Office] projects in its report on a single-payer plan that government spending on health care would increase substantially. They go on to say to cover the massive cost of government-run care, income taxes would have to at least double. Income taxes, American families — at least double," Barrasso said.

SHOCK POLL: TALARICO TIES PAXTON IN TEXAS SENATE RACE, THREATENING GOP STRONGHOLD

Talarico’s campaign did not address questions on whether his designs for healthcare are shaped by the national deficit, but noted that his plan includes increases in taxes on the country's top earners.

"James supports making billionaires pay their fair share so we can cut taxes for middle class Texans and fund healthcare for working families — which is why he has unveiled plans to end special tax handouts to corporations and billionaires to help fund healthcare, while proudly voting for the largest property tax cut in Texas history to make sure middle class families get a break," the Talarico campaign told Fox News Digital. "Ken Paxton has worked to enrich himself and his billionaire mega-donors, amassed 15 properties on a taxpayer-funded salary, and was impeached by his own party for his corrupt abuse of office."

Having cleared the party primary, Talarico will face off against Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton in the state’s Nov. 3 general election.

item.title: Chiefs owner's wife Tavia Hunt has heard enough about how they get all the calls and she's sick of it
item.description: Tavia Hunt shared film of Chris Jones being held during the Raiders game, pushing back on claims that the Kansas City Chiefs get all the calls.
item.content:encoded:
Tavia Hunt, wife of Kansas City Chiefs owner Clark Hunt, has heard all about how her team gets all the calls and she's had enough. She pushed back on that narrative on social media earlier this week.

Is her opinion biased? It could be, but she's taken a look at the stats and studied the film according to her statement on the matter.

In a post on Tavia's Instagram story, where I'd argue these sorts of matters should be settled, she shared a clip of Chiefs defensive lineman Chris Jones being held in the end zone while Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins surveys the field for an open receiver. See the alleged missed call here.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"So sick of the past narrative that the Chiefs get all the calls," she wrote. "Stats don’t lie and neither does film — so I’m leaving this here."

The Chiefs ended up winning the game 30-27 and improved to 4-0. I'm sure there were missed calls that went the Chiefs way during the game as well as there are in every game.

BRITTANY MAHOMES TROLLS RAIDERS AFTER LAS VEGAS COACH SEEMED CERTAIN TEAM WOULD BEAT CHIEFS

Winning three Super Bowls over a five-year span is going to add some fuel to the "Chiefs get all the calls" fire. And so does a study the NY Post reports was conducted by the University of Texas at El Paso in October 2025.

They found that "postseason officiating has disproportionately favored the [Patrick] Mahomes-era Kansas City Chiefs, coinciding with their rise as one of the NFL’s most marketable franchises."

Now, so far this season, the numbers, according to the NY Post, are more on Tavia and the Chiefs side.

The part of this whole back-and-forth over whether they get all the calls or not that is being lost is that some people don't care what the numbers are. They enjoy getting the Chiefs fans all the way up to the wife of the owner of the team riled up by claiming that they get all the calls.

It's really the little things in life that give people true joy.

item.title: Mike Waltz fights back tears revealing what Hamas hostage refused to do before release
item.description: Eliya Cohen, freed after 505 days in Hamas captivity, and Nova festival survivor Ziv Abud shared their harrowing stories at the United Nations.
item.content:encoded:
UNITED NATIONS — Three years after the worst massacre in Israel’s history, Eliya Cohen — who survived 505 days in Hamas captivity — took the stage at the United Nations alongside his newlywed wife, Ziv Abud, a survivor of the Nova music festival massacre, and tried to explain to some of the world’s top diplomats what he had endured.

"They didn't let me change clothes or to get a shower, even to eat or to drink," he said. "They chained me with heavy iron chains by my leg," Cohen said during an emotional discussion moderated by Dr. Phil McGraw at Israel’s U.N. commemoration Tuesday.

He said lights were kept on to prevent the hostages from sleeping and that captors would enter repeatedly during the night screaming in an effort to frighten them. Cohen said they were not permitted to use a restroom and that at times survival felt almost impossible.

FREED HOSTAGE ROM BRASLAVSKI DETAILS ABUSE, STARVATION DURING 738 DAYS IN GAZA CAPTIVITY

But he described repeatedly forcing his mind away from the violence and toward the possibility of returning home.

"Don't think about the violence. Don't think about the torture. Don't think about everything," Cohen recalled telling himself. "Just continue, stay strong. And maybe one day, you will come back home to your family."

Cohen was among the 251 people abducted during the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attack, when about 1,200 people were killed in southern Israel in their homes and at the Nova Music festival. It was the deadliest single day in Israel’s history. He personally lost 48 people he knew that day.

His wife, Ziv, carried a different piece of the same story.

Abud and Cohen had arrived at the Nova festival shortly before dawn with her 19-year-old nephew Amit and his girlfriend Karin. When the attack began, they eventually took refuge in a roadside bomb shelter that Cohen said was designed for roughly eight people but became packed with 29.

HAMAS USED SEXUAL VIOLENCE 'DELIBERATELY AND SYSTEMATICALLY' ON OCT 7, COMMISSION REPORT FINDS

Abud told the audience that more than 40 terrorists later attacked the shelter with grenades and gunfire. One man inside repeatedly grabbed grenades and threw them back outside before he was killed, she said.

As the attack continued, Cohen covered Abud with bodies — an act that saved her life.

"I lost my consciousness. Eliya was kidnapped," Abud said. "And after seven hours, I woke up in the shelter. I found myself in a pile of bodies."

She paused, fighting back the tears. "It wasn't even bodies. It was body parts."

Abud said she then saw that Amit and Karin had been killed. "I needed to sit with the bodies for seven more hours," she said. She was eventually rescued, one of seven survivors from the shelter.

"We were four people that went to the festival from the same house," Abud said, "And I'm the only one that came back home that night."

FORMER HAMAS HOSTAGE COUNTERS HASAN PIKER’S UT AUSTIN EVENT WITH HER STORY OF SURVIVAL

For 505 days, she campaigned for Cohen’s return without knowing whether the man she loved would ever come home. Cohen, meanwhile, said he believed while in captivity that Abud had been killed.

The couple married weeks before Tuesday’s ceremony.

"But now he's here," Abud said. "And I can look forward to the future after we got married."

She said she hoped the years ahead would include "kids and family because we are here and we survived. And we need to live a normal life," she said.

Another Oct. 7 survivor who addressed the diplomats was Oriya Berlin, a young Israeli visual intelligence observer who had arrived at a base in the Gaza border area just two days before the attack.

Berlin said she woke on the morning of Oct. 7 believing she was hearing a thunderstorm.

"Outside, thousands of missiles were raining down with a single objective: to destroy my life and the lives of my friends," she said.

Berlin and four other soldiers ran barefoot and in pajamas into a small shelter. They were unarmed. She said the women initially believed the incursion would resemble scenarios they had studied during training — a small squad that Israeli forces could quickly contain.

Seconds later, she said, they heard vehicles and gunfire. Berlin described roughly 60 heavily armed terrorists attacking the base. At one point, she said, a message appeared in the unit’s WhatsApp group telling soldiers to shout "IDF" in Hebrew so Israeli troops could find them. The broken Hebrew immediately raised suspicions that a terrorist had taken a soldier’s phone.

They remained silent.

Berlin said they then heard another group shouting for soldiers to identify themselves, followed by a burst of gunfire and silence.

Ten hours after the attack began, she said, special forces finally reached them.

THE SENATE HAS REMEMBERED AMERICA’S OCTOBER 7TH VICTIMS. NOW IT’S TIME TO HEAL

Berlin said that after learning how many of her friends had been murdered or kidnapped, she could not remain at home. Although she was offered the opportunity to leave military service, Berlin said she refused and returned as an observer for another six months before later moving into the IDF Public Diplomacy Office.

"I wanted the world to see that the IDF is not just an intimidating military force on a television screen," she said. "It was also a 5'2" fake blonde girl like me who simply wanted to protect her home, her family, and her friends."

She said she has since spoken before audiences ranging from international organizations to high school students who told her "I was wasting their time because of their deep-seated anti-Israel hostility." "But I stayed," Berlin said. "I spoke because the truth demands a voice."

Berlin said her decision to continue speaking was rooted in the friends who did not survive.

Before the ceremony, U.S. Ambassador to the U.N. Mike Waltz met privately with Cohen and Abud, asking Cohen how he was feeling physically and telling the couple how good it was to see them "healthy and alive."

Minutes later, from the stage, Waltz became visibly emotional as he recounted a part of Cohen’s captivity that he said he had been unable to get out of his mind.

Waltz said that on the night before Cohen’s release, Hamas tried to make him record a propaganda video claiming he had been treated well. "He refused," Waltz said. "He held firm. He said no."

Waltz said Hamas again tried to turn Cohen’s release into propaganda the following day, placing him before cameras and instructing him to raise his hands.

"He refused again," Waltz said. "Eliya, we salute you. I salute you," Waltz continued. "You are a proud, strong Jew. You're undefeated, man" he said with his voice breaking.

The hostage crisis stretched over two years and several rounds of negotiations, releases and rescue operations. Waltz told Fox News Digital after Tuesday’s ceremony that he wanted the commemoration to acknowledge both the loss of Oct. 7 and how much had changed since.

"Oct. 7, 2023, was their 9/11, was their Pearl Harbor," Waltz said. "More Jews were brutally massacred that day than any day since the Holocaust."

ISRAELI OCTOBER 7 SURVIVORS CONQUER TRAUMA ALONGSIDE LEGENDARY ROCK ICONS IN POWERFUL NEW DOCUMENTARY

He said it was important "to recognize the loss" and "hear directly from the survivors," but also to take stock of the region three years later.

"We have President Trump's 20-point peace plan. We have a U.N. resolution establishing the International Stabilization Force," Waltz told Fox News Digital. "He's determined to not repeat what's happened so often in the past, where Hamas rebuilds, Iran rearms, they attack again, and you have this devastation all over again."

Waltz pointed to broader shifts across the Middle East.

"Iran is on its back foot. Lebanon has hope, Syria has hope. Iraq has hope," he said.

He said he hoped the commemoration could combine "remembrance, the perspective, and I think charting, trying to chart a path of hope and peace for the future."

From the stage, Waltz argued that Oct. 7 had produced the opposite strategic result from what Iran and its allies sought. "Oct. 7 completely, and I think irreversibly, has backfired on Iran and all of their terrorist proxies," he said, pointing to changes in Syria, Lebanon and Iraq and the expansion of Israel’s regional relationships.

He ended with a message to the audience: "America will stand with the Jewish people."

"Be strong. Be resilient. Be wise," Waltz said. "And know that what you're doing is right. Stand with your moral compass and know that this administration, the United States of America, stands with you."

Israeli Ambassador to the U.N. Danny Danon used the gathering — attended by ambassadors and diplomats from multiple countries — to turn his attention to the institution hosting it.

MOTHER OF OCTOBER 7 HOSTAGE WHO WAS EXECUTED UNPACKS HER GRIEF IN NEW MEMOIR

"Even in this building, the U.N. is trying to demonize and isolate Israel," Danon said. "They have turned the victim into the accused, comparing our IDF soldiers to Hamas terrorists."

Danon said he has been told by colleagues that he takes criticism of Israel at the U.N. ‘too personally’.

"Indeed, it is personal," he responded. "My daughter is serving right now in the IDF. My son served as an officer in the IDF," Danon said. "He was supposed to be on the Re'im base next to Gaza on Oct. 7. The last minute, he was released home for the holiday."

"That's why it's personal," Danon said. "The U.N. tries to demonize all of our sons and daughters, our lions and lionesses who give everything so we can freely live in our homeland. So yes, it is personal. It's personal for all of us."

For Cohen and Abud, however, the event eventually returned from geopolitics to something much smaller: the possibility of an ordinary future.

Abud said they hoped to have children and build a family despite knowing that Oct. 7 and the 505 days that followed would remain part of their lives.

Cohen, asked by McGraw what he would say if the terrorists who abducted and tortured him were watching, needed only a few words.

"I won," Cohen said.

"I won and I'm here."

He then turned his message outward.

"Stay proud to be Jewish," Cohen said. "And stay proud to be Israeli."

"We are here to stay."

item.title: The best defense against high-tech AI scams is low-tech skepticism, expert warns
item.description: Cybersecurity expert Morgan Wright says human skepticism remains the strongest defense against AI-driven phishing scams and voice cloning fraud schemes.
item.content:encoded:
As artificial intelligence rapidly evolves to make financial scams hyperrealistic, cybersecurity experts warn that the best defense isn't sophisticated detection software.

It's good old-fashioned human skepticism.

While adversarial states like China and Russia leverage AI on a global scale, average Americans are most frequently targeted by cybercriminals looking to exploit personal vulnerabilities for a quick payout, according to cybersecurity expert Morgan Wright.

"Let's go back to around 1860, when Edgar Allan Poe wrote, ‘Believe nothing that you hear and only one half that you see,’" Wright told Fox News Digital. "That advice is as good now as it was 160 years ago."

AI VOICE SCAMS CAN CLONE YOUR FAMILY’S VOICE

AI technology has allowed bad actors to automate and scale personalized fraud schemes against everyday citizens. Generative tools eliminate language barriers, draft convincing phishing texts and generate hyperrealistic voice and video clones.

By capturing just a few seconds of audio — often scraped from social media — fraudsters can convincingly replicate the voice of a family member. Wright pointed to the case of Deborah Del Mastro, a California mother who lost thousands of dollars after scammers used AI to clone her daughter’s voice to stage a terrifying kidnapping hoax.

THE FAMILY GROUP CHAT IS A GOLDMINE FOR SCAMMERS

"It's my daughter's voice," Del Mastro recalled during an interview on The CyberGuy Report podcast. "And she's having a panic attack."

Convinced her daughter was in immediate danger, Del Mastro transferred more than $5,000 to the scammers before realizing she had been swindled.

FRAUD EXPERT WARNS AI IS HELPING CRIMINALS OUTPACE THE GOVERNMENT: 'DON'T HAVE THE RIGHT TOOLS'

"When you can fool a mother, that's how good these things are getting," Wright said of the voice-cloning technology. "What they do is use manipulation, influence and deceit. The more urgent I can make it sound, the more you're going to lower your guard and take action."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE U.S. NEWS

Wright, who has trained federal, state and local law enforcement in behavioral analysis, interviewing and interrogation — including teams at the FBI and the National Security Agency — emphasized that every scam relies on basic psychological triggers.

His primary advice for anyone on the receiving end of a suspicious call or message is to pause before reacting.

"We're not storming the beaches at Normandy; you're not going to get arrested," Wright said. "No law enforcement agency sends you an unsolicited text saying you're about to get arrested."

While AI platforms roll out updated security features, scammers continuously find ways around them, making software-based detection a constant moving target.

"We hear about all the different models from xAI, Anthropic, OpenAI and Gemini. They change models constantly," Wright said. 

"So, when the model changes, how effective is [detection software]? We don't know because this stuff is moving so fast. What you see today will be drastically different tomorrow."

item.title: Amy Klobuchar calls for major anti-terrorism investments after alleged Mall of America plot
item.description: Amy Klobuchar praised the FBI after an 18-year-old was arrested for allegedly plotting an ISIS-inspired mass shooting at the Mall of America.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Amy Klobuchar, the Democratic nominee for Minnesota governor, praised law enforcement Wednesday after the FBI arrested an 18-year-old man accused of plotting an ISIS-inspired mass shooting at the Mall of America.

"I'm grateful for the heroic work of law enforcement that prevented a mass shooting and terrorist attack at the Mall of America," she said in a statement. "This shows why we continue to need major coordinated investments in anti-terrorism and local law enforcement to stop attacks like these. Our state must take terrorism and violent crime head on, working with our federal law enforcement and local police departments to keep Minnesotans safe."

Klobuchar, who has represented Minnesota in the U.S. Senate since 2007, is running against Republican Minnesota House Speaker Lisa Demuth in the November gubernatorial election.

MALL OF AMERICA TERROR PLOT THWARTED, SUSPECTED ISIS SYMPATHIZER ARRESTED, FBI ANNOUNCES

Her statement came after federal authorities announced the arrest of Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud, 18, who investigators say pledged allegiance to ISIS and discussed carrying out a mass shooting at the Mall of America.

According to federal court documents, Mohamud allegedly spent months discussing plans for an attack before buying an AK-47-style rifle, four magazines and roughly 200 rounds of ammunition from an undercover FBI employee Tuesday. The rifle had been rendered inoperable, though the ammunition was live.

FBI Director Kash Patel said Mohamud "allegedly obtained a weapon he hoped to use in a mass casualty attack in support of ISIS, but this FBI arrested him and put a stop to his plans."

PENNSYLVANIA MAN ACCUSED OF PLOTTING ISIS ATTACK ARRESTED WITH RIFLE AND 190 ROUNDS OF AMMUNITION: DOJ

President Donald Trump also praised the FBI’s handling of the case while speaking to reporters Wednesday.

"I did hear about it. And they did a great job. The FBI did a great job," Trump said.

Mohamud is charged with knowingly receiving a firearm and ammunition while knowing or having reasonable cause to believe they would be used to commit a felony and federal crime of terrorism.

Fox News Digital's Stephen Sorace and Paul Steinhauser contributed to this report.

item.title: California education candidate tells college professors to teach students basic math, rejects SAT requirement
item.description: Richard Barrera told UC professors it's their job to teach students who arrive without basic math skills, drawing sharp criticism from California superintendent opponent Sonja Shaw.
item.content:encoded:
California state superintendent candidate Richard Barrera drew criticism Tuesday from his opponent and education advocates after telling UC professors it was their job to teach students who arrive without basic math skills and rejecting the return of standardized testing requirements as the University of California confronts growing concerns over college readiness.

Barrera, president of the San Diego Unified School District Board of Education and a senior policy advisor to state superintendent Tony Thurmond, made the comments during a Sunday interview with NBC Los Angeles political reporter Conan Nolan. Barrera was asked whether the SAT should return as a requirement for the UC system as professors raise alarms about students entering elite universities without foundational math skills.

"Absolutely not," Barrera said. "So math teachers at UCLA and Berkeley and every place else, part of your job that you get paid by the taxpayers to do is to teach our kids."

Barrera told Fox News Digital that concerns about UC students being unable to perform basic math were "completely overstated," arguing that some incoming students instead just need review in subjects they had not studied recently, and that universities shared responsibility for helping them catch up.

UNPREPARED COLLEGE STUDENTS FORCED TO RELEARN 'MIDDLE SCHOOL MATHEMATICS,' CALIFORNIA PROFESSORS REVEAL

"I do think that this idea that students are coming in not knowing fractions is completely overstated," Barrera said. "What we're seeing is students who take a placement test, in the summer before they attend their freshman year at UC, who might miss questions on algebra, on trigonometry, maybe subjects that they haven't had in a couple of years. That's just about review and acceleration."

"This is not about students who are incapable of doing the work," he added. "This is about students who need some review and acceleration, and it is the responsibility of UC to participate in that acceleration."

Chino Valley Unified School District Board President Sonja Shaw, Barrera's opponent in the November race for state superintendent of public instruction, told Fox News Digital that his response shifted responsibility away from California's K-12 education system.

"Richard Barrera heard professors at Berkeley and UCLA sound the alarm that incoming students can’t do elementary-school math and his immediate response was to blame the professors. Not the students. Not the system that passed them along. The professors," Shaw said. 

"His brilliant solution? Force college faculty to teach remedial middle-school math on the taxpayer dime, and claim that bringing back the SAT is somehow ‘exclusionary,’" she added. "That’s not a plan. That’s a career politician scrambling to cover up a failure he helped create."

Corey DeAngelis, a research fellow at The Heritage Foundation, told Fox News Digital that Barrera's opposition to standardized testing protected California's K-12 education system from accountability for students reaching college without foundational math skills.

"Richard Barrera’s answer tells you everything you need to know about who he works for. The California Teachers Association is bankrolling his campaign for state superintendent, and he is returning the favor by protecting the system from accountability," DeAngelis said.

WATCHDOG REPORT EXPOSES TEACHERS UNION 'POLITICAL MACHINE' FUNNELING MORE THAN $1 BILLION TO LIBERAL CAUSES

Nolan followed up by asking Barrera whether professors at some of the country's leading universities should be responsible for teaching students fractions. Barrera said some students had overcome significant obstacles to reach those campuses.

"Listen, we've got students who are coming up from incredible experiences, first-generation students overcoming so many barriers to be on the campus," Barrera said. "Those students are capable of learning quickly. What they need is a little support to be caught up. What they don't need is to be excluded."

Tina Descovich, CEO and co-founder of Moms for Liberty, told Fox News Digital that students arriving at college without foundational skills reflected problems that began years before they reached a university classroom.

"A child who can't do fractions at 18 was a child who couldn't do fractions at ten, and the system knew it," she said. "Richard Barrera's solution is to make it a college professor's problem and continue to cover up the failures of the status quo. Parents in California have watched their kids get passed along for years. Now they're being told the people who did the passing along deserve a promotion."

GAVIN NEWSOM AVOIDS QUESTION ON BRINGING BACK SAT SCORES AFTER UC OPEN LETTER, ASKS 'SHOW ME THE DATA'

The exchange came months after more than 1,400 faculty members signed an open letter calling for SAT and ACT math requirements to be restored for STEM applicants. By August, more than 3,000 faculty members had signed letters raising concerns about academic preparation.

California's state testing results show a similar proficiency gap before students reach college. According to the state's 2024-25 Smarter Balanced assessment results, 30.49% of 11th graders met or exceeded the standard in mathematics, compared with 56.96% in English language arts.

DeAngelis said that those results undercut the argument that students reaching college without foundational math skills merely need additional support once on campus.

"About 30 percent of California 11th graders meet math standards," he said. "That result is not a story about first-generation students who just need a little catch-up once they reach campus. That failure is a system that handed out diplomas without requiring mastery, then blamed the score for noticing."

Barrera defended his opposition to restoring the SAT or ACT requirements in UC admissions, saying that concerns about students needing additional academic preparation predated the university system’s decision to eliminate standardized tests and arguing the exams had historically excluded some applicants.

"It's not the elimination of the SAT, you know, that is what we need to look at," Barrera said. "The question that we all need to be asking ourselves is, what are the best strategies to get students prepared for college-level math? And simply having a placement exam like the SAT, which is historically discriminatory towards students of color, towards first-generation students — it's a tool that has historically excluded students." 

"Why would we reinstitute that, knowing that that has shown no relevance in helping improve students' preparedness for college-level math?" he added.

The UC Board of Regents' current admissions policy prohibits SAT and ACT scores from being used in its comprehensive admissions review, but the university system is now formally reconsidering standardized testing.

Shaw said that the state should instead focus on whether students master core subjects before reaching college.

"Students are not helped by being lied to about their skills," she said. "They’re helped by actually learning to read, write, and do math before they get to college. That requires high standards in K-12 enforced consistently and measured honestly." 

"It does not mean turning UCLA and Berkeley into expensive elementary schools and then blaming the faculty for noticing the problem," she added. "Lowering the bar one more time will not fix a decade of failure. It will just hide it longer."

item.title: Comedy stars lash out at Sebastian Maniscalco over SiriusXM shake-up
item.description: Comedians like Patton Oswalt and Michelle Wolf are urging Sebastian Maniscalco to reverse a SiriusXM channel rebrand they say hurts working-class comics.
item.content:encoded:
Sebastian Maniscalco has found himself in hot water with some comedians who are claiming that his new SiriusXM channel is taking away money and exposure from working-class comics.

Earlier this year, SiriusXM changed a long-running channel in its lineup called Raw Comedy that often featured lesser-known comedians to Sebastian Maniscalco's Comedy Radio. The new station more prominently features famous comedians now. 

Stand Up for Stand Up, a nonprofit that supports comedians, recently wrote an article saying the rebranding has "drastically shifted from a wider pool of 800-plus comedians enjoying spins (and thus, royalties and exposure to the audience of listeners)" on the channel "to a narrower pool of comedians getting plays per month. 

"And of those few hundred who are getting spins, over 75% of the plays are going to the top 50 artists, which results in a concentration of wealth among the top echelon, which is largely made up of big-name celebrity comics."

SEBASTIAN MANISCALCO IS A NO-NONSENSE FATHER, SAYS PARENTS NEED TO BE 'HALF-PSYCHOTIC' WITH THEIR KIDS

The nonprofit called the change "bad for comedians, and bad for the future of comedy," adding, "it hurts passive revenue, and discoverability, as well as the infrastructure that supports up and coming comedians."

Comedian Matt Ruby on his Substack page claimed the channel was "crushing middle class comedians who rely on payments from the company to pad income."

Liz Miele, another comedian, said in a video on her Instagram, "This year, the Raw channel on SiriusXM became Sebastian Maniscalco’s channel. Great. Fine. Celebrities have taken over channels before. Never been an issue. The problem is Raw went from playing 800 working-class comedians to now playing less than 300 celebrity comedians like Joan Rivers, Johnny Carson, Bob Hope, Norm Macdonald. Just dead comic, dead comic, dead comic, and then a plethora of very famous alive comedians that might not even know about this extra income that they’re about to receive."

She added that every "working-class comedian that has been kicked off the channel is quite aware" of the money they've lost. 

Comedian Gianmarco Soresi posted a photo of Maniscalco on X with the caption, "Aren’t you embarrassed?"

Comedian Ashley Ray, who relied on the income, wrote on X, "Those checks went from covering a car payment to barely covering a quarter of weed, i hate this man."

COMEDIAN SEBASTIAN MANISCALCO JABS CANCEL CULTURE WITH ST PATRICK'S DAY MESSAGE

Famous names like Patton Oswalt, Michelle Wolf and Margaret Cho also implored Maniscalco to do something this week.

"I know you didn’t mean to do anything bad by doing it. You can easily reverse this decision. Get those young comedians back on the Sirius channel," Oswalt said in a Facebook video. "Let them get those checks."

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Wolf also pleaded with Maniscalco in a Facebook video, saying, "Comics, we’re together on this. We want it to change."

"Sebastian, give working comedians a chance," Cho said in a video on her Facebook.

Others took to social media to defend Maniscalco.

"Sirius radio did this not Sebastian," one X user wrote. "Jesus Christ the dude is always there for young comics."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Another user said, "TBH this likely has little to do with him, his name is just on the channel. Altho I do miss when Raw Dog was actually raw w/some of the edgiest comics."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

"His reps think this is gonna blow over — and they're right," a third added.

"The amount of comedians that think Sebastian Maniscalco is a program director is f---ing sad," another person wrote on X. "He sold his name to be on the channel hes not deciding who gets played."

In a statement to Fox News Digital, SiriusXM said, "SiriusXM works together with our creative partners to program the best possible experience for our listeners. 

"The launch of Sebastian Maniscalco’s Comedy Radio introduced a new creative direction and a regularly evolving programming mix for the channel, and SiriusXM continues to invest in comedians more than any other audio platform to deliver a wide range of comedy offerings across our channels."

The company said in a press release announcing the new channel in April that the channel would be "curated and headlined by Maniscalco."

Fox News Digital has reached out to Maniscalco for comment.

item.title: Ohio high school football team pulls off the most amazing half of football ever & the wokes want Sophie FIRED!
item.description: First Hump Day of October Nightcaps features an Ohio high school football team that possessed the ball for all 24 minutes of the second half.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

First Hump Day of October? Sign me up!

We're in the thick of it now, boys and girls. Today is the final day with four MLB games back-to-back-to-back-to-back until ... who knows when? Next March? Next May? 2028? It's anyone's guess. Enjoy it.

We've also got two college football games tonight, NFL tomorrow and a whole slate of both on Saturday and Sunday. It's all ahead of us right now, folks. Let's lock it in, and not waste a single second.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SENDS A MESSAGE TO THE WOMAN-HATING WNBA PLAYERS WITH HER HAT, CRANKY PRIME & MAGGIE SAJAK!

Let's roll.

Welcome to a Hump Day Nightcaps — the one where a high school football team in Ohio pulled off maybe the most amazing half of football I've ever seen.

Spoiler alert: They managed to possess the football for all 24 minutes. Every single one of them. Animals.

You'll see!

What else? I've got an update on the NASCAR driver who owes an ex-wife $850K after seducing her husband, the wokes are mad at Sophie Cunningham and Caitlin Clark for two hilarious reasons and we've got two postseason pitchers taking very different approaches to the birth of their children this week.

Shockingly, it's caused quite a stir on social media. That almost never happens. We're always so agreeable!

OK, grab you a Fluffernutter in preparation for tomorrow's National Fluffernutter Day, and settle in for a Hump Day 'Cap!

Look at that commercial. Man, what a time to be alive. Watch that, and then pay attention to the garbage we get in between innings of today's baseball game(s).

It's shocking. It's so sad. Our creativity has just gone down the toilet.

Pathetic.

Anyway, I do love a good fluffernutter. Admittedly, it's been, easily, 20 years since I've had one, but man they were elite back in middle and high school. I assume fluff has been all but canceled in today's MAHA world, which is fine. I live with a MAHA mom. Trust me, I get it.

FLORIDA HIGH SCHOOL FOOTBALL GAME ERUPTS INTO VIOLENT BRAWL INVOLVING PLAYERS, COACHES AFTER FINAL WHISTLE

But goodness gracious, they were the best back in the day. Opening up your brown bag in the middle school cafeteria and seeing that mom packed you a fluffernutter sammy was the best feeling.

Simpler times.

OK, let's stay in grade school and get this class started with a couple Ohio high school football team playing keep-away from each other last Friday night.

Amazing:

I went back and watched the entire second, and can confirm that Fairmont did indeed possess the ball all 24 minutes. I've never seen anything like it.

Just ground-n-pound the length of the field — twice — and execute a pair of onside kicks. Wild stuff. Reminded me of my high school's old Wing-T offense.

Those games were absolute slobberknockers every single time. I miss the heck outta them.

Now, some folks are asking about the onside kicks...

The first "onside" kick wasn't visible on the above YouTube stream because the video froze, but the announcers did call it an onside kick.

The second one wasn't so much an onside kick as it was the kicker just drilling the opposing player in front of him and Fairmont pouncing on the ball. Not sure if that was the plan or not, but it worked out.

Regardless, the final stats are staggering:

I covered a lot of high school football back in the day. I don't think I missed a Friday night in seven years. I came semi-close to one of these games back in 2015 when I watched a huge underdog just run the wildcat for an entire quarter. They gained about three yards per carry, and then converted all the fourth downs. It was incredible. Ate up almost 12 straight minutes.

What a game. What a sport. High school football is the best.

You know what's NOT the best? Cheating on your spouse in a Comfort Inn and letting the whole hotel know about it:

So, I wrote about that in last Thursday's Nightcaps, and I'm happy (?) to report that we have our smoking gun in the case.

According to court records obtained by the Daily Mail, the ex-wife of longtime NASCAR spotter Clayton Hughes hired a private investigator months before the two divorced. The PI, Jim Rorie, told a court that he heard Jennifer Jo Cobb and Hughes having "rambunctious" sex in a Comfort Inn on Oct. 2020 after he followed him to the hotel via a tracking device planted on his car.

"There was no doubt about what I was hearing," he told a court, adding that he heard "the squeaking of the bed, quite a bit of that, female tones moaning — and occasionally a male’s voice.

"As the squeaking continued, the tones of a male moaning and saying, ‘Oh f–k’ and ‘Oh my God’ were distinctly heard," Rorie continued. "I believe there was one point where I heard the female yell, ‘Don’t stop.'"

Welp. Probably not the worst thing to happen in a Comfort Inn in Martinsville, but it's certainly up there!

OK, let's rapid-fire this Hump Day class into a big Hump Day night. First up? Let's see how the miserable wokes are handling Day 3 of the Indiana Fever's offseason ...

Let me get this straight ...

You've got one insufferable columnist from the woke New York Times saying Sophie Cunningham should be cut because she's too much of a distraction ... because she told ESPN six months ago that men shouldn't be in women's locker rooms?

Okeedokee!

At the same time, you have someone I've never heard of in my life, Charlotte Wilder, getting all bent out of shape because Caitlin Clark hung out with Pat McAfee on College GameDay?

Really?

These people are so far gone, and so beyond broken, it's almost unfathomable.

Almost.

What a bunch of weirdos. We live in such a silly time period. My late grandfather always used to tell me, "You really do realize how [stupid] people are the older you get."

He did NOT use the word stupid, by the way, but I'll let y'all figure that one out on your own.

OK, on the way out, I want to leave the class with a question that's currently dividing the internet ...

If your wife is having your baby in October, are you missing playoff baseball games for it?

So, the best closer in baseball — Mason Miller — missed last night's do-or-die Game 3 for the birth of his child. Meanwhile, Yankees starter Max Fried says he ain't missing a single pitch for the birth of his kid.

Where we stand on this, folks? On one hand, these dudes get paid handsomely for these moments. For October baseball. For the playoffs.

On the other hand ... it's the birth of your child. That's a big deal ... for some, at least.

I wanna hear what YOU think. Let it RIP.

See y'all tomorrow.

Lemme know! Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.

item.title: Paramore's Hayley Williams targets Christian nationalism as America's 'greatest threat' to democracy
item.description: Hayley Williams called Christian nationalism the greatest threat to American democracy at a recent concert, drawing sharp pushback.
item.content:encoded:
Paramore frontwoman Hayley Williams faced criticism after telling fans during a September concert that Christian nationalism is "the greatest threat to American democracy," adding another political declaration to a tour where she had repeatedly spoken out against President Donald Trump, immigration enforcement and Israel's war in Gaza.

In the recirculated clip, Williams made the declaration before performing "True Believer," a track from her 2025 solo album, "Ego Death at a Bachelorette Party." 

Her statement specifically targeted Christian nationalism, rather than Christians or Christianity broadly.

"The greatest threat to American democracy is Christian nationalism," Williams said.

ED SHEERAN CONCERTGOERS WARN ARTISTS ABOUT SHARING POLITICAL VIEWS: 'YOU'RE GOING TO ALIENATE' FANS

Lisa Cusack, president of the Don’t L.A. My Burbank PAC, told Fox News Digital that Williams’ comment ignored Christianity’s influence on the nation’s founding principles and democratic system.

"Incredibly ignorant comment considering Christianity is woven into the fabric of every founding document that proscribes Americans' democratic rights," she said. "There would be no Natural Law without Christianity, and without that, no human rights that exist beyond a government’s power. Christianity sees all people as made in the image of God, so are all valuable, no matter how successful, and puts self-sacrifice above power."

"Democracy has thrived in the Christian nations across the world for a reason. The true threat is this kind of ignorant bigotry," she continued.

item.title: Dolly Parton’s nephew erupted in profanity-laced tirade in emails days before her death
item.description: Bryan Seaver's expletive-filled emails about Nashville hotel security surfaced in court documents filed just days before Dolly Parton's death.
item.content:encoded:
Dolly Parton’s nephew unleashed an expletive-filled tirade in an email exchange involving the country music legend just days before her death as tensions over security services boiled over, according to court documents obtained by Fox News Digital.

Bryan Seaver, Parton's nephew and longtime head of security, fired off the profanity-laced message Aug. 21, four days before Parton's death, in an email chain carrying the subject line "Fwd: Letter from Dolly."

"Hi Billy. Message received," Seaver began. "If you think my harsh language is too much for your failing vendors to digest, just wait until my lawyers start f---ing you up the a--."

DOLLY PARTON’S SISTERS PUSH BACK ON FEUD RUMORS AFTER NEPHEW’S LEGAL BATTLE WITH STAR'S ESTATE ERUPTS

While it's unclear who Billy is, Parton’s longtime manager, Danny Nozell, and other members of her team were included in the email chain.

"I challenge you to bring spurious and feeble complaints. Let’s play ball you f---ing s---bag loser," he continued.

Seaver also blasted the progress of an apparent Nashville project, alleging the build-out was "late and worrisome" and subcontractors "continue to do drugs in our venue."

"Explain to your shareholders why your project is still failing and your building is unfinished, unoccupied and mired in violations," he wrote.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Seaver ended the blistering message with another warning.

"I encourage it. Go f--- yourself you f---ing weakling," he wrote. "Tell Mr. [redacted] to call me and we’ll talk man to man. Otherwise, your doom ensues."

The court exhibit does not reveal the contents of the apparent "Letter from Dolly" referenced in the subject line.

DOLLY PARTON’S SISTER REVEALS ‘LAST THING’ COUNTRY LEGEND ASKED OF HER BEFORE DEATH

The email came just two days after Seaver directly invoked his famous aunt while complaining about security arrangements at a Nashville hotel project.

"Your contract security company (Titan) you’ve hired in spite of me and Dolly’s request for service at the hotel has completely f---ed up and let an employee be assaulted," Seaver alleged in the Aug. 19 email.

"Let me know when you are ready to hand the security situation completely over to Dolly’s contracted service providers in Nashville and I will fix your problem," he added. "SAPS (Seaver’s Squadron Augmented Protection Services) is your answer."

The combative exchanges marked a dramatic shift from correspondence less than three months earlier.

On May 29, Seaver offered to help staff and train security personnel in Nashville. The recipient, identified as "Bill," thanked him for his "genuine care and concern" and said he hoped both teams would support "each other in success."

Parton died Aug. 25 at age 80 after a brief battle with cancer.

Seaver, who had served as Parton's head of security for more than two decades, was chosen by his aunt to publicly announce her death. Less than a month later, tensions between Seaver and members of Parton's business circle spilled into court.

As Fox News Digital previously reported, Parton's manager, Nozell, who runs She’s Alive, LLC, sought a restraining order against Seaver and his company, Squadron Augmented Protection Services.

She's Alive is an entity Parton created to oversee her business interests.

DOLLY PARTON LAID TO REST AS NIECE SHARES EMOTIONAL TRIBUTE TO ‘GRANNY’

A Tennessee judge granted a temporary restraining order, citing an alleged pattern of threats and demands for payment, along with Seaver's "claimed access to weapons, experience with violence, and intention to retaliate." The order barred Seaver and his company from entering She’s Alive properties, coming within 1,000 feet of its employees and business partners or contacting them.

She’s Alive alleged Seaver's communications continued to escalate after Parton's death.

In a Sept. 1 message included in earlier court filings, Seaver allegedly threatened to start a podcast aimed at damaging Parton's business relationships unless he was paid.

According to documents previously obtained by Fox News Digital, the alleged messages prompted several employees to resign, Parton's trust and estate attorney to step away and She’s Alive to hire private security to protect employees at work and at home. Seaver was fired Sept. 15 over what the company characterized as "terrorizing conduct."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Seaver has denied threatening anyone and maintained that his communications were taken out of context.

"I've never threatened anyone," Seaver previously told ABC News, calling the restraining order "spurious and simply a publicity stunt."

The newly surfaced emails show that tensions involving Seaver, Parton's business interests and security arrangements had been escalating even before the singer's death.

In an Oct. 5 filing, attorneys for She’s Alive specifically pointed to the communications, arguing that Seaver had not disputed sending them.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"He has not denied that he sent any of the texts or emails attributed to him," the attorneys wrote.

Those assertions were made by She’s Alive and were not findings by the court.

The filing also accused Seaver of attempting to evade service, claiming a process server tried three times to serve him. During one attempt, four vehicles were spotted in his driveway, but no one answered the door. The filing said his residence later had a "no-trespassing" sign in the yard and barbed wire draped across the handrails leading to the front door.

On Oct. 6, Chancellor I’Ashea L. Myles granted Seaver additional time to obtain counsel and rescheduled a hearing for Oct. 20. The temporary restraining order will remain in effect through the hearing.

Parton's sister Freida has publicly defended her nephew amid the legal battle, insisting there is "no feud within our family" and adding, "We all love Bryan, just as we all love each other."

Fox News Digital's Larry Fink and Lauryn Overhultz contributed to this report.

item.title: Florida GOP hopeful on backing Trump in Iran: 'This is about ending a long war, not starting a war'
item.description: Florida GOP candidate Dan Green explains his positions on Iran, immigration and fiscal policy, arguing his views align more with the 9th District than those of Dem Rep. Darren Soto.
item.content:encoded:
For GOP congressional candidate Dan Green, the military confrontation with Iran isn't the start of a new war — it’s the long-overdue resolution of a conflict that began in 1979. 

Drawing on his own military tours in Iraq, the Navy veteran running in Florida’s 9th Congressional District argues that America is finally settling decades-long strife with Tehran, even as he faces a tough domestic battle over inflation, kitchen-table economics and a 10-year Democrat incumbent in the newly redrawn Orlando-based suburban district.

"I think one thing to know about Iran is that they've been at war with us since the 1970s, when they seized our embassy in Tehran and they took our Americans hostage. So to me, this is about ending a long war, not starting a war. 

"Whether it's the Marine Corps barracks in the '80s when Iran bombed those, the Khobar Towers in Saudi Arabia, and also with my tours in Iraq, the Iranians were killing a lot of our soldiers, sailors, airmen and Marines.

TOP DEM LEGAL BOOGEYMEN TEE UP 'BATTLE ROYALE' IN RED STATE'S REDISTRICTING CRUSADE

"So, the question is, what's the butcher's bill you're willing to tolerate of dead Americans? And we also know they plotted to kill and assassinate our president. 

"So, to me, this has been a long time coming, but I think what we really need to focus on is how do we get a successful termination of this conflict and stability back in the Middle East?"

Green is running in a district that voted for President Donald Trump by a large margin in 2024, yet the Republicans face headwinds as inflation and energy prices remain a persistent preoccupation for voters. Yet, he remains confident in the appeal of the GOP brand, compared to the Democratic alternative.

"I think the Democrats have a huge problem right now. I don't think they know what they're really about," Green said. "As you know, they have a democratic socialist wing that is rising in power throughout their party, and a lot of moderate members are finding they have to make peace with that, or even liberal members as well."

He continued: "We've got a lot of members getting elected now across the country who are democratic socialists who believe in this radical ideology, who want to frankly destroy our Constitution in so many ways: they want to abolish the U.S. Senate, they want to bring back woke ideology, transgender ideology, and higher taxes. So I think in some ways we know what they are going to bring, but it's not a good future."

GOP CHALLENGER TEARS INTO DEM'S ‘MODERATE’ IMAGE: ‘VOTES WITH THE SQUAD 90% OF THE TIME’

Florida's 9th District, like much of the state, contains a large Latino population, which has been pivotal in shifting the state from purple to red. Green argues that while Republicans must appeal to voters on kitchen table economics, ultimately they need to be the party that upholds the rule of law.

"I think Americans of all backgrounds, regardless of race or ethnicity, are concerned about the cost of living these days. What we've been campaigning on is making America affordable again," Green said. "So these kind of kitchen table issues of grocery prices, gas prices, property insurance rates — they resonate irrespective of background, I would say. 

"But the cornerstone of our republic is the rule of law, making sure we adhere to it and we follow it. There are ways of being compassionate with how we do that. There are ways of implementing that law more effectively. At the end of the day, we're either a nation of laws or we aren't. And so we need to do what's required to make sure the law is enforced."

The 9th District, which stretches from Orlando to the south, has a distinctly conservative bent, which Green argues will enable him to compete against the advantages of incumbency.

FLORIDA GOP NOMINEE BLASTS 20-YEAR DEM INCUMBENT AS A ‘SOCIALIST’ RUBBER-STAMP WITH ’PRECIOUS LITTLE TO SHOW'

"My opponent is an incumbent and sometimes with that come some advantages; name ID, access to greater resources," Green said. "But I think the district fundamentally is a conservative district and I think even non-party-affiliated members who aren't Democrat or Republican tend to be conservative.

"So I think we have a lot of great strength in this district for our campaign. I have worked in the military, I can put a plan together, and we're executing a good campaign plan to take the seat back and flip it from blue to red."

Finally, Green said he believes Soto's votes on economic policies will be key to building a contrasting vision for the voters of the 9th District.

"Well, he's been re-elected from a portion of our district, not the rest of the district. Most of the district has never voted for him or really seen him," Green said. "To me, you've got a decade of not solving our district's problems. 

"He has voted against eliminating taxes on Social Security. He's voted against eliminating taxes [on] overtime. He's voted against eliminating tax on tips. To me, when you have the sort of affordability issue right now, those are not the right votes to take for this district. His values are also not aligned with our voters, as well. 

"You know, he voted to not prohibit transgender care. He's also not done anything to stop insider trading for 10 years… and also, frankly, the democratic socialists are taking over the Democratic Party. You know, a vote for him is a vote for them, and I think that's not what this district wants."
